item.title: About
item.content:encoded:
About

We think of architecture not as a single practice, but as several interlocking ones. Landscapes are inseparable from structures, ecology is inseparable from building requirements, and improving human relationships is the ultimate goal of any project. Aesthetic movements come and go, but we have found these principles to be timeless.

As partners, we strive for honesty and clarity. Our first job is to understand the client’s vision and needs, not to present our own. We value timeliness, direct communication and prototypes over presentations, as well as the occasional face-to-face meeting over a drink or a meal.

Over the years, we have been fortunate to collaborate with some excellent clients on some wonderful projects, but we believe it is still too early to weigh in on the success of the work. A building exists in time and its usefulness is directly related to how well it continues to perform.

We are proud of our Danish home and heritage, but do not consider ourselves exponents of Danish design. National style has no place in architecture, where a building must first and foremost be suited to local needs.

Whether you are a professional video maker or a newbie, below-mentioned are the amazing techniques that you should follow to come up with exceptional video. They are simple, easy and doable. They will get you results you need and even better. So, read all and follow each.

1. Always be original.

Don’t fake. I would repeat over and again be who you are and never showcase any falsity when making video. The more you stay with originality, the more you can assure about good results. It is as simple as it can be. On the contrary, when we say to add unoriginality, it actually means that you need to put a lot more efforts and exertions.

Come up with the original and creative concept of your video project means saying no to others’ notions of perfections and staying away from stealing other creative ideas. All you need to conduct persona and keyword research, get wind of the type of video content that is not only popular but also you think will be successful in your industry. Once you get done with the concept, check again if the concept doesn’t seem similar to another brand.      

2. Plan it out.

No matter what you do and which field you belong to, the one thing you cannot deny is planning can benefit you in so many ways. It is simple and easy. Start with your script. Pen down creative plot. Draw out a storyboard. And, then come up with a shot list. Don’t forget to plan your b-roll shots as this can give you an extra footage when it comes to editing.

Here, I need to clear out that writing a script for your video is not as same as writing a blog post. And, if you are considering both as same, you need to think again.

3. Check yourself.

Each and everything matters when it comes to crafting a video content and filing it. It is quite easy to make a silly mistake, but you need to avoid them in any cost, as these can rub away all your efforts in no time. To avoid such mistakes, you need to be mindful about everything you do, and then make sure over and again everything is performed with utmost care.

To ensure accuracy and correctness, make use of playback during the interview to review everything that you have filmed and make sure if you actually need retakes. Don’t be reluctant to do more than one take for key sections.

4. Time-lapse

A well-known technique, time-lapse is widely used but still not very well developed. It is a perfect way to display the time and illustrate it quite effectively when done properly in conjunction with a normal installation. It will introduce you to a spot, show the transformation from one day to another and show you something which is evolving whether it is a building project or a farm.

So, what are you waiting for? Be prepared to make an exceptional thing!

It is often a misconception that creativity is about the wing and the moment one way or another. But relating this with filmmaking is not wise. The best way is to get prepared as a professional video maker. Tools like storyboards can also allow you to have a solid base.

Last but not least, always remember that if you do something amazing you can contribute to it on the day, if you fail to do so, you'll only be faced with your main storyboards. So, choice is yours…

item.title: How to Start Up Your Own Post Production Companies
item.content:encoded:
Getting afraid and confused with the entire procedure of starting up a post-production company on your own is quite obvious. It is not a piece of cake to start your own business and make it a big success. Neither is it impossible. Throughout the route, you will have to deal with a lot of challenges. Some days you will even curse yourself making a decision to open the company, some days you would be hopeful about the positive results. Basically, everything depends on you and what you choose.

This piece of writing covers everything from the memorable name of a producer to the oceans of paperwork that you have to swim through to make the most of every effort you made and get profit.

So, let’s take the bull by the horns.

﻿

1. Start with a plan

A detailed plan or approach is key to make headway. It will allow you to map and uncover nonentities about your area of interest. You need to raise several questions here. The one is about the growth and operating costs. Another one is about your target audience, your break time and your name of your company.

2. Establish a legal entity

Establish a legal organization. It can protect you from being directly responsible for the actions of your film producing business. Also, you are suggested to take helpful assistance from an agent service. Make sure the agent is certified and reliable enough to save you from all the hassles.

3. Register for taxes

Before open for a business, register for a number of state and federal taxes. Apply for an EIN to file for taxes. It's not difficult to register. The IRS web site allows you to obtain your EIN free of charge by fax or by mail.

4. Open a bank account & credit card

For personal asset security, the importance of specialist corporate banks and credit accounts is irrefutable. Unless your record gets messed up, your financial properties, your house, your vehicle and other valuables, are at risk in case your firm gets sued.

5. Acquire required documents  

The next and important step is the acquisition of important documents. These may include necessary permits, licenses and business insurance. In case you fail to obtain any of these documents, you will have to pay a hefty amount as fine, which you surely don’t want to. These fines can even harm your newly-formed business.

6. Describe your brand

What reputation your company holds and how it works – everything depends on your brand. Your brand is what your people think about you and your business. This means you can make a good impression on your customs with a good brand. And, even you can stand out from your rivals.

Starting up your business, as said above, is complex. When you fight for contracts, sales, and even the business, you will mentally and financially drain. Fortunately, this foundational guide, carrying important steps and ideas, can save you and allow you to reach your goals.

Content development for a fruitful marketing campaign is already a tricky business, add a video to it, and you've just upped your game for a problematic marketing gimmick. Since the modern marketing industry has switched from just static pictures to more animation and video-related content, it would be highly effective if you went through a couple of marketing video production tips. While these may be targeted for a marketing video, they may, however, be used to ensure quality video production for any other purpose as well.

﻿﻿

Originality of Content

Marketing is something that requires ingenuity more than any other business management field. While your organization may be operating profitably with products similar to a competitor, it's highly probable they would face a backlash if a marketing campaign lacks novelty. To avoid this, it is increasingly significant for you to choose highly original content. Original content for a marketing video has the highest chances of getting to the targeted audience with precisely the motive it was produced for.

Choice of Content

Make wise choices for content – You can't go displaying a Viagra being sold by a priest, the two are "incomprehensible" together, even though there's no harm. But it's just how people perceive the product and the person differently. So when you make a marketing video, you've got be extra cautious when selecting the content and don't just go making an absurd video. A wise choice of material for the marketing video has a chance to make sales soar higher by nearly 50% – 70%.

Location Selection

Avoid "set dressing" – for a marketing video or any other video, make sure you have a location that you are trying to portray. Or else don't go for it. Set dressing is something which is bound to diminish the video's purpose more than you can perceive. Don't try to set up a seaside on your rooftop! Content Alignment

Don't just merge various clips and upload the video for your brand. You can't imagine the backlash that coming your way, and with a more advanced option for people, you might just be the next content for trolls. So make sure that all your clips and the content has magnificence embedded in its alignment. Review the video multiple times, edit it to perfection and ensure that you've got a third-person available to review it for any glitches which would show alignment errors.

Video Optimization

Optimization of the video is essential, both the text and the video and the all-over video with a platform where you might be uploading it. You might be uploading the video on social media and the television as well, but make sure that you know that it is optimized accordingly. An audience difference exits between the two platforms, which might cause the marketing campaign to face criticism and lose the initially intended purpose. Similarly, you don't want your subtitles or other textual content going haywire over unintended visuals of the video. Thorough checks are beneficial for you to ensure that the marketing video has got the quality to reach the audience with the initially intended purpose.

item.title: The Magic of Color Correction in Video Editing
item.content:encoded:
What is color correction? 

Colors play an important role in illustrating your images and videos; they can define the intensity of the emotions of the characters or anything displayed in the subject. But correct light and scenic conditions are pricey and may become out of reach for many. This is when color correction video editing comes into play.

In post-production, the process of color correction is carried out. Generally, videos are shot in a flat setup, so the detailing can be preserved without alteration. At first, a video shot in a flat format is very dull and boring, but it provides control over the final product using the video editor since they are less constrained. We can change the image's color range, as well as its sharpness, brightness, saturation, and contrast. The difference between the original picture and the final product is always the opposite.

 

Why is it done?

The most rudimentary type of color correction is to give a uniform color space for multiple video samples. A shoot is often done over a few days, and the differences in each day's color and lighting will affect the videos. These variations can be reversed, so there is a clear color palette in the final product. The changes can be made more dramatic.

Often, there are specifications on where the video will be displayed; most stations have color standards that have to be followed. Color correction guarantees that no information or details are lost when watching the video on different TVs and platforms.

Most video editors are using color correct to play with it more than just a regular touch-up. It is widely used to set the tone using color correction, which ultimately helps to express a message overall. If they're filming an ad for a college, they could increase the video's saturation and brightness, bringing out the building and grass colors, giving it a happy and cheerful feeling. But if they're making a post-apocalyptic film, that might make the picture darker and less saturated. Make things more boring and less dull. A film's color palette may be made subtle, but it can make a big impact on the audience.

For example, some films will have night scenes in daylight, this saves on lighting equipment and then darken it in post-production. This is a very popular tool for feature films because it prevents the least lack of raw data.

Additionally, color correction may be used to mimic other film cameras or eras. DSLR cameras are economical than commercial film cameras, but a high-broadcast camera can change the defined coloring of DSLR images to look like it was filmed in the shot eras. Historical videos can be changed in such a way that the picture quality and look are in line with the period seen on it.

Keeping all these factors in mind, we can conclude that color correction is a crucial part of film and media production.

MindInMotion Video Productions FAQ’s

How much does a video cost in Orlando?

Most projects land in three tiers: $2.5-5K (lean crew, single shoot day, simple deliverables), $5-$20K (most common), $20K+ (larger crew/locations/talent and multiple shoot days)

What kinds of videos do you produce?

TV/OTT spots, social ads, brand films, product videos, corporate/exec interviews, and non-profit marketing videos —with deliverables for broadcast + all socials.

How fast is turnaround?

Standard delivery is within 7-14 days, more complicated projects may require additional time, and rush edits are available upon request.

Do you handle permits and locations in Orlando?

Yes. We scout, pull permits when required, and recommend film‑friendly spots across Downtown, Winter Park, Lake Nona, Kissimmee, and beyond.

Can you plug into our agency or in‑house team?

Totally. We can jump in for production only or handle end‑to‑end from brief through post.

Optional. We enjoy the process of working with our clients in person but we understand you can’t always be there and we are able to provide a remote client video feed if needed.

Do you shoot broadcast and social cutdowns?

Yes— we can provide multiple edits/aspect ratios (16:9, 1:1, 9:16).

Where do you operate?

All of Central Florida: Orlando, Winter Park, Lake Nona, Celebration, Kissimmee, Sanford, Altamonte Springs, and along I‑4.

Can you handle casting, VO, and music?

Yes—local on-camera/VO casting, session direction, and properly licensed music.

Do you offer accessibility options (captions/subtitles)?

Yes—open or closed captions, SDH, and translated subtitles.

Can you work with our existing footage or user generated content?

Yes—happy to ingest, organize, and integrate provided assets (we’ll audit quality/compatibility first).

We serve Orlando, Kissimmee, Sanford, Winter Park, Altamonte Springs, and the Lake Nona Region!
